inlines.text: 以新工具和新支持加强打击网络儿童性虐待

blocks.text: 新工具、实用指南和合作伙伴关系将有助于预防、检测和应对网络儿童性剥削与性虐待。

inlines.text: 新工具、实用指南和合作伙伴关系将有助于预防、检测和应对网络儿童性剥削与性虐待。

blocks.text: 分享

inlines.text: 分享

blocks.text: 今天，我们发布了一款新工具，用于检测儿童性虐待材料（CSAM），同时推出能够打断有害行为并引导人们寻求帮助的干预措施、面向开发者的实用资源，以及对儿童安全执法调查人员的支持。这些工作建立在我们的儿童安全蓝图以及持续开展的检测、拦截和举报虐待行为的工作基础之上。对家长来说，目标很简单：让技术帮助保护儿童安全，同时由人来掌控。

blocks.text: 众所周知⁠(opens in a new window)⁠(opens in a new window)，打击网络儿童侵害者需要众多组织协同合作。像 OpenAI 这样的单个公司有责任防止我们的技术被侵害者利用来伤害儿童，我们也必须与更广泛的行业、儿童安全组织和执法部门携手，共同推进保护儿童上网安全的集体努力。

blocks.text: 帮助更多组织检测虐待材料

inlines.text: 帮助更多组织检测虐待材料

blocks.text: 我们在现有防护措施的基础上，发布了一款新的图像分类器，能够检测潜在的 CSAM，包括 AI 生成的材料。这款新分类器会寻找虐待的视觉迹象，帮助团队识别此前可能从未见过的新型图像。它会返回评分，帮助审核人员判断哪些图像可能需要优先处理。这是首个广泛可用、并能明确提示 CSAM 是否可能由 AI 生成的 CSAM 分类器。

blocks.text: 我们的团队在美国国家失踪与受虐儿童中心（NCMEC）⁠(opens in a new window)的协助下训练、评估并设计了这款分类器，使其能够投入实际部署。NCMEC 是一家非营利组织，运营着 CyberTipline——一个集中受理网络儿童剥削举报的平台。

blocks.text: 我们通过 OpenAI API 向经过审核的组织免费提供这款分类器的访问权限，让儿童安全组织和更广泛的行业（包括团队规模各异的组织）更容易获得 CSAM 检测能力。

blocks.text: 儿童安全是全行业的问题，需要各组织之间紧密协作，并采取多种解决方案。我们已与Tech Coalition⁠(opens in a new window)和ROOST⁠(opens in a new window)接洽，帮助我们共享这款新工具的访问权限；我们也大力支持由其他机构开发的工具，例如Thorn 的 Safer⁠(opens in a new window) CSAM 检测系统。此外，我们最近开始参与 Tech Coalition 的Lantern 计划⁠(opens in a new window)，将在其中共享并接收与网络儿童性剥削和性虐待相关的信号，以加强跨平台协作。

inlines.text: SafetyKit

blocks.text: “儿童安全工具需要识别不同类型内容中的虐待行为。在我们的测试中，OpenAI 的分类器是我们见过最好的，能捕捉哈希匹配漏掉的未知 CSAM，在绘画和动画上表现强劲，对合法成人内容的误报率低于 1%。这些令人鼓舞的结果表明，可以在限制对合法用户干扰的同时，提供更广泛的防护来抵御有害内容。”

blocks.text: 打断有害行为，引导人们寻求帮助

inlines.text: 打断有害行为，引导人们寻求帮助

blocks.text: 我们已禁止 CSAM，训练模型拒绝相关请求，并对违反政策的账号采取行动。在此基础上，我们在 ChatGPT 中新增产品警告：当用户试图寻找虐待性内容时予以打断，说明后果，并引导其寻求帮助以停止有害行为。

inlines.text: 我们已
禁止 CSAM
，训练模型拒绝相关请求，并对违反政策的账号采取行动。在此基础上，我们在 ChatGPT 中新增产品警告：当用户试图寻找虐待性内容时予以打断，说明后果，并引导其寻求帮助以停止有害行为。

blocks.text: 警告会明确指出，将儿童性化会造成伤害，即使所请求的内容是 AI 生成的也不例外。除警告外，我们会删除被标记的对话，并暂停该用户访问 ChatGPT 24 小时，同时保持专业支持渠道可用，帮助人们停止有害行为。屡次违规可能导致更长时间的限制，最终可能关闭账号或向有关部门举报。

blocks.text: “OpenAI 在 ChatGPT 中提供了一个最佳实践范例，展示平台如何遏制并打击有害的在线行为。OpenAI 邀请了多位曾设计并评估过警告信息的外部专家，与他们一起通过基于证据的协同设计打造了这项干预措施，并力求在尽可能多的司法管辖区把用户引导至当地的支持资源。这让警告信息最有可能引导用户远离伤害、转向支持。”

inlines.text: Lucy Faithfull Foundation

blocks.text: “从我们的威慑工作中我们知道，一条警告能否奏效，取决于时机、准确性和语气。OpenAI 在这三点上都下了真功夫。这条警告会在人们面临风险的当下打断他们，直白地说明后果，并指引他们寻求帮助。重要的是，当风险行为持续时，响应会变得更加强硬。我们的 Stop It Now 求助热线已经经常接到有人说，是 AI 聊天机器人把他们引导到我们这里来的。如今这条求助途径正在走向全球，把人们连接到他们本国的支持资源。每一个选择主动求助、而不是顺从冲动行事的人，都是一个被保护的孩子。”

blocks.text: 为开发者提供实用支持

inlines.text: 为开发者提供实用支持

blocks.text: 保护儿童上网安全并不止于检测。我们发布了 CSAM 指南⁠（在新窗口打开），为开发者提供切实可行的步骤，用来预防虐待、检测有害内容并采取行动。该指南在制定过程中采纳了 Tech Coalition⁠（在新窗口打开）、Thorn⁠（在新窗口打开）、NCMEC⁠（在新窗口打开） 和 Internet Watch Foundation⁠（在新窗口打开） 的意见，面向处于安全系统建设不同阶段的组织。

blocks.text: 指南给出了明确的规则、用户报告疑虑的途径、检测工具，以及审查和上报疑似虐待行为的流程。它还说明了安全标识符如何帮助开发者将滥用行为关联到具体用户，以及如何为审查敏感内容的人员提供支持。开发者可以将它与我们的新图像分类器、Moderation API⁠（在新窗口打开）、ROOST 的自托管审查控制台 Coop⁠（在新窗口打开），以及 Thorn 的 Safer⁠（在新窗口打开） 等专门的 CSAM 检测服务配合使用。

blocks.text: 支持儿童安全执法部门

inlines.text: 支持儿童安全执法部门

blocks.text: 保护儿童也意味着为专门从事儿童安全调查的人员提供支持，帮助他们找到受害者、制止虐待行为。正如我们与 Thorn 公开讨论过的（在新窗口打开），AI 可以帮助调查人员整理和排序信息，减少不必要地接触虐待材料。

blocks.text: 继续携手推进

inlines.text: 继续携手推进

blocks.text: 这些努力有着共同的目标：防止儿童受到伤害，并在虐待发生时加强应对。我们将继续完善防护措施，同时为儿童保护组织、开发者、研究人员和调查人员提供所需的工具、资源和专业知识，帮助他们保护儿童、打击剥削并将施害者绳之以法。通过携手合作，我们可以借助 AI 的力量，在打击儿童性剥削和性虐待的斗争中带来切实的改变。

blocks.text: Strengthening the fight against online child sexual abuse with new tools and support

inlines.text: Strengthening the fight against online child sexual abuse with new tools and support

blocks.text: New tools, practical guidance, and partnerships will help prevent, detect and respond to online child sexual exploitation and abuse.

inlines.text: New tools, practical guidance, and partnerships will help prevent, detect and respond to online child sexual exploitation and abuse.

blocks.text: Share

inlines.text: Share

blocks.text: Today, we’re releasing a new tool to detect child sexual abuse material (CSAM), interventions that interrupt harmful behavior and point people toward help, practical resources for developers, and support for child-safety law enforcement investigators. These efforts build on our Child Safety Blueprint and our ongoing work to detect, block, and report abuse. For parents, the goal is simple: technology that helps keep children safe, with people in control.

inlines.text: Today, we’re releasing a new tool to detect child sexual abuse material (CSAM), interventions that interrupt harmful behavior and point people toward help, practical resources for developers, and support for child-safety law enforcement investigators. These efforts build on our

ongoing work to detect, block, and report abuse

blocks.text: It is well⁠(opens in a new window)established⁠(opens in a new window) that combatting online child predators requires coordination across many organizations. Individual companies like OpenAI have a responsibility to prevent our technology from being exploited by predators to harm children, and we also must work together with the broader industry, child safety organizations and law enforcement to advance our collective efforts to protect children online.

blocks.text: Helping more organizations detect abusive material

inlines.text: Helping more organizations detect abusive material

blocks.text: We’re building on our current protections with the release of a new image classifier that can detect potential CSAM, including AI-generated material. This new classifier looks for visual signs of abuse, helping teams identify novel images that may not have been seen before. It returns scores that help reviewers decide which images may need attention first. This is the first CSAM classifier with broad availability that has a specific signal on indicating if CSAM may be AI generated.

blocks.text: Our teams trained, evaluated, and designed the classifier for real-world deployment with assistance from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC)⁠(opens in a new window), a nonprofit that operates the CyberTipline, a centralized reporting hub for the online exploitation of children.

blocks.text: We’re offering access to the classifier to vetted organizations through the OpenAI API at no cost, making CSAM detection more accessible to child safety organizations and the broader industry, including those with teams of varying sizes.

blocks.text: Child safety is an industry-wide issue that requires strong collaboration across organizations and a variety of solutions. We’ve engaged the Tech Coalition⁠(opens in a new window) and ROOST⁠(opens in a new window) to help us share access to this new tool, and we are strong supporters of tools developed by others such as Thorn’s Safer⁠(opens in a new window) CSAM detection system. In addition, we recently began participating in the Tech Coalition's Lantern program⁠(opens in a new window), where we will share and receive signals relating to online child sexual exploitation and abuse to strengthen cross- platform collaboration.

blocks.text: Early access partners have also evaluated how the classifier supports their own safety teams. In fal⁠(opens in a new window)’s testing on human-reviewed production images, reviewers confirmed 72% of the classifier’s high-confidence flags as novel CSAM. invideo AI⁠(opens in a new window)’s testing showed one in four flagged cases led to a ban. In SafetyKit⁠(opens in a new window)’s evaluations involving drawings or animations that sexualize children, the classifier detected 90% of cases.

These encouraging results point to broader protection against harmful content while limiting disruption for legitimate users.”

blocks.text: Interrupting harmful behavior and pointing people toward help

inlines.text: Interrupting harmful behavior and pointing people toward help

blocks.text: We already prohibit CSAM, train our models to refuse requests for it, and take action against accounts that violate our policies. We’re building on those safeguards with new product warnings in ChatGPT that interrupt attempts to find abusive material, explain the consequences, and point people toward help to stop harmful behavior.

, train our models to refuse requests for it, and take action against accounts that violate our policies. We’re building on those safeguards with new product warnings in ChatGPT that interrupt attempts to find abusive material, explain the consequences, and point people toward help to stop harmful behavior.

blocks.text: The warning makes clear that sexualizing children causes harm, including when the requested material is AI-generated. Alongside the warning, we’ll remove the flagged conversation and pause access to ChatGPT for 24 hours, while keeping specialist support available to help people stop harmful behavior. Repeated violations may lead to longer restrictions and ultimately account closure or reports to authorities.

blocks.text: CSAM Deterrence Centre

inlines.text: CSAM Deterrence Centre

blocks.text: “OpenAI has deployed a best-practice example in ChatGPT of how a platform can deter and disrupt harmful online behaviours. OpenAI has engaged multiple external experts who have previously designed and evaluated warning messages, built the intervention with them through evidence-based co-design, and aims to redirect users to local support options in as many jurisdictions as possible. This has given the warnings the best chance of steering users away from harm and towards support.”

blocks.text: Lucy Faithfull Foundation

inlines.text: Lucy Faithfull Foundation

blocks.text: “We know from our deterrence work that a warning succeeds or fails on timing, accuracy and tone. OpenAI has taken real care with all three. It’s a warning that interrupts people at the moment of risk, speaks plainly about the consequences, and points them to help. Importantly, the response becomes stronger when risky behaviour continues. Our Stop It Now helpline already regularly hears from people who say an AI chatbot sent them to us. Now that route to help is going global, connecting people to support in their own country. Every person who reaches out instead of acting on their impulses is a child protecte d.”

blocks.text: Practical support for developers

inlines.text: Practical support for developers

blocks.text: The protection of children online doesn’t end with detection. We’ve published CSAM guidance⁠(opens in a new window) to give developers practical steps to prevent abuse, detect harmful content, and act on it. Developed with input from the Tech Coalition⁠(opens in a new window), Thorn⁠(opens in a new window), NCMEC⁠(opens in a new window), and the Internet Watch Foundation⁠(opens in a new window), it is designed for organizations at different stages of building their safety systems.

blocks.text: The guidance provides clear rules, ways for users to report concerns, detection tools, and processes for reviewing and reporting suspected abuse. It also explains how safety identifiers can help developers connect misuse to individual users and how to support the people reviewing sensitive content. Developers can use it alongside tools such as our new image classifier, Moderation API⁠(opens in a new window), ROOST’s self-hosted review console Coop⁠(opens in a new window), and dedicated CSAM detection services such as Thorn’s Safer⁠(opens in a new window).

blocks.text: Our commitment to collaboration and supporting the broader developer ecosystem also is reflected in our work with Anthropic and Google to jointly commission new guidance on responding to disclosures of child sexual exploitation and abuse in AI systems. Recently published by the Tech Coalition⁠(opens in a new window), this guidance provides developers with practical recommendations for addressing these sensitive situations.

blocks.text: Supporting child-safety law enforcement units

inlines.text: Supporting child-safety law enforcement units

blocks.text: Protecting children also means supporting the specialist child safety investigators working to find victims and stop abuse. As we’ve discussed publicly with Thorn⁠(opens in a new window), AI can help investigators organize and prioritize information and reduce unnecessary exposure to abusive material.

blocks.text: We’re also supporting child-safety law enforcement units with new tools and trainings on how to use AI in their investigations, including dedicated plugins, investigative tools, and complex data analysis, with access managed by program administrators. At launch, the first tool will help investigators review lengthy chat logs and legal process returns, identify potential connections, and create timelines, with findings linked to source material.

blocks.text: The initial training is planned as an overview and demonstration, supported by a practical field guide that teams can refer to afterward. It will introduce the tools and how they fit into investigative work. Access will depend on agency authorization and program requirements. Future iterations of the training will be proposed at regional, national and international conferences.

inlines.text: North Carolina Attorney General

blocks.text: “As state attorneys general on the AI Task Force, our first priority is protecting kids. That needs to be the first priority of tech companies too. We must increase our defenses, and OpenAI and other tech companies must be thinking about and working around the clock to prevent synthetic child sex abuse material. We need to keep our children safe.”

blocks.text: Continuing the work together

inlines.text: Continuing the work together

blocks.text: These efforts share one goal: preventing harm to children and strengthening the response when abuse occurs. We’ll continue improving our safeguards while empowering child protection organizations, developers, researchers, and investigators with the tools, resources, and expertise they need to protect children, combat exploitation, and bring perpetrators to justice. By working together, we can harness the power of AI to make a meaningful difference in the fight against child sexual exploitation and abuse.
